Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether uniform integrability of $\{|X_t|^p : t \ge 0\}$ implies uniform integrability of $\{X_t : t \ge 0\}$.

**Answer: Yes.**

**Proof.**

The hypothesis is that the family $\{|X_t|^p : t \ge 0\}$ is uniformly integrable. A uniformly integrable family has bounded $L^1$-norm, so
$$M := \sup_{t \ge 0} \mathbb{E}[|X_t|^p] < \infty.$$

We show $\{X_t : t \ge 0\}$ is uniformly integrable, i.e., $\sup_{t \ge 0} \mathbb{E}[|X_t|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_t| > K\}}] \to 0$ as $K \to \infty$.

**Case $p = 1$.** Then $|X_t|^p = |X_t|$, so the hypothesis gives UI of $\{|X_t|\}$ directly, hence $\{X_t\}$ is UI.

**Case $p > 1$.** For $K \ge 1$ and any $t \ge 0$:
$$\mathbb{E}[|X_t|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_t| > K\}}] = \mathbb{E}\big[|X_t|^{1-p}\cdot|X_t|^p\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_t| > K\}}\big].$$
On the event $\{|X_t| > K\}$, since $1 - p < 0$, we have $|X_t|^{1-p} \le K^{1-p}$. Therefore
$$\mathbb{E}[|X_t|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_t| > K\}}] \le K^{1-p}\,\mathbb{E}[|X_t|^p] \le K^{1-p}\,M.$$
Taking the supremum over $t \ge 0$:
$$\sup_{t \ge 0} \mathbb{E}[|X_t|\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|X_t| > K\}}] \le K^{1-p}\,M \;\xrightarrow{K \to \infty}\; 0,$$
since $p > 1$ (so $1-p < 0$) and $M < \infty$. This establishes uniform integrability of $\{|X_t|\}_{t \ge 0}$, hence of $\{X_t\}_{t \ge 0}$.

**Remark.** The argument only uses the boundedness $\sup_t \mathbb{E}[|X_t|^p] < \infty$ (a consequence of UI), not the full strength of UI. The continuity and local martingale properties of $X$ are not needed; the result is purely a consequence of the $L^p$-bound and the domination $|X_t| \le K^{1-p}|X_t|^p$ on $\{|X_t|>K\}$ for $p>1$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
